name: Audio-Technica AT2020 Microphone
description:
The Audio-Technica AT2020 is a side-address condenser microphone with a wide dynamic range and high SPL handling — perfect for home studio recording, vocals, and podcasting.

Used by Tachy for all vocal tracking. Delivers crisp, professional-quality sound at an affordable price point.
seoTitle: Audio-Technica AT2020 Microphone — Studio Gear Recommended by Tachy
seoDescription: Buy the Audio-Technica AT2020 condenser microphone recommended by Tachy for home studio recording, vocals, and podcasting.
features: Cardioid polar pattern reduces background noise
Frequency response: 20–20,000 Hz for detailed sound capture
Handles high SPL up to 144 dB — great for loud sources
Requires 48V phantom power (standard with any audio interface)
Includes stand mount and protective pouch
whyRecommend:
I've been using the AT2020 since my first home studio setup. For the price, it's hands-down the best entry-level condenser mic on the market. The cardioid pattern isolates my vocals beautifully even in an untreated room, and the high SPL handling means I never have to worry about distortion when tracking loud takes.

If you're just starting your home studio journey, this is the first mic you should buy.

faq.question: Do I need an audio interface for this microphone?
faq.answer: Yes, the AT2020 requires 48V phantom power, which is provided by any standard audio interface like the Focusrite Scarlett 2i2.

faq.question: Is this microphone good for podcasting?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Its cardioid pattern picks up sound from the front while rejecting room noise, making it excellent for spoken word and podcasting.

faq.question: What cable do I need?
faq.answer: You need a standard XLR cable (male to female). The microphone does not use USB — it's a professional XLR connection.

name: Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 (4th Gen)
description:
The Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 4th Gen is the industry-standard audio interface for musicians and producers. Two pristine mic preamps, ultra-low latency, and loopback functionality.

Tachy uses this as the centerpiece of his portable recording rig. Compatible with all major DAWs.
seoTitle: Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 (4th Gen) — Audio Interface by Tachy
seoDescription: Buy the Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 4th Gen audio interface. Industry-standard USB-C interface for home recording and music production.
features: 2-in / 2-out USB-C audio interface with ultra-low latency
Air mode enhances vocal presence with a high-frequency lift
High-impedance (Hi-Z) instrument input for guitar and bass
Loopback functionality for streaming and podcasting
Includes Ableton Live Lite and Pro Tools | First
whyRecommend:
The Scarlett 2i2 is the first piece of gear I recommend to anyone building a home studio. It's what I started with, and it's still in my portable rig today. The 4th Gen preamps are noticeably cleaner than previous versions — my vocals come through with zero noise floor.

Air mode is a game-changer: one click and your vocal track instantly sits better in the mix. Plus, the USB-C connection means it works flawlessly with modern laptops.

faq.question: Does this work with my DAW?
faq.answer: Yes, the Scarlett 2i2 is class-compliant and works with all major DAWs including Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio, Cubase, Pro Tools, and GarageBand.

faq.question: Can I use this for streaming?
faq.answer: Yes! The 4th Gen includes loopback functionality, which lets you route audio from your computer back into your stream — perfect for streaming and podcasting.

faq.question: Does it come with any software?
faq.answer: Yes, it includes Ableton Live Lite, Pro Tools | First, and a suite of Focusrite plugins and effects.

name: Shure SM7B Dynamic Microphone
description:
The Shure SM7B is a legendary dynamic microphone with a smooth, flat, wide-range frequency response — the go-to choice for vocals, broadcasting, and podcasting worldwide.

Features an advanced air suspension shock isolation and pop filter built-in. Tachy's preferred mic for live-streaming and voiceovers.
seoTitle: Shure SM7B — Professional Dynamic Microphone by Tachy
seoDescription: Buy the Shure SM7B dynamic microphone. Legendary vocal and broadcasting mic with built-in pop filter and shock isolation.
features: Dynamic cartridge with smooth, flat frequency response
Cardioid polar pattern rejects off-axis noise
Built-in pop filter and air suspension shock isolation
Detachable windscreen included for close-up vocals
Legendary broadcast sound used by professionals worldwide
whyRecommend:
The SM7B is my go-to microphone for streaming and voiceover work. Unlike condenser mics, it doesn't pick up every tiny room sound — which is crucial when you're recording in a less-than-perfect space.

The built-in pop filter and shock mount mean you don't need any extra accessories. Just plug it in and your voice sounds broadcast-ready. It's an investment, but one that will last you a decade or more.

faq.question: Do I need a cloudlifter with the SM7B?
faq.answer: The SM7B has low output. With modern audio interfaces like the Scarlett 2i2 4th Gen, a cloudlifter is optional but recommended for cleaner gain.

faq.question: Is this good for music vocals?
faq.answer: Yes, the SM7B has been used on countless hit records. It delivers a warm, present vocal tone that sits well in a mix without harshness.

faq.question: Does it require phantom power?
faq.answer: No, the SM7B is a dynamic microphone and does not require phantom power. It works with standard XLR connections.

name: AKG K240 Studio Headphones
description:
The AKG K240 Studio is a semi-open, over-ear reference headphone trusted by audio engineers worldwide for mixing and monitoring.

Lightweight, comfortable for long sessions, and delivers a natural, balanced sound. Tachy relies on these for final mix checks before release.
seoTitle: AKG K240 Studio Headphones — Mixing & Monitoring by Tachy
seoDescription: Buy the AKG K240 Studio semi-open reference headphones. Trusted for mixing and monitoring with natural, balanced sound.
features: Semi-open design provides natural spatial imaging
Varimotion 30mm XXL drivers for detailed sound
Self-adjusting headband for all-day comfort
55 ohms impedance — works without a headphone amp
Detachable mini-XLR cable for easy replacement
whyRecommend:
These headphones are incredible value. I use the K240s for late-night mixing sessions when I can't use my monitors. The semi-open design gives you a natural stereo image that helps you place each element in the mix accurately.

They're also incredibly comfortable — I've worn them for 6-hour sessions without any fatigue. At this price point, every producer should own a pair.

faq.question: Do I need a headphone amplifier?
faq.answer: At 55 ohms, the K240s can be driven by most audio interfaces and laptops, though a dedicated headphone amp will give you more headroom.

faq.question: Are these good for mixing?
faq.answer: Yes, they're widely considered one of the best budget mixing headphones. The semi-open design gives a wide soundstage for critical listening.

faq.question: Do they leak sound?
faq.answer: As semi-open headphones, they do leak some sound and let in ambient noise. They're best suited for quiet listening environments.

name: Rode NT1-A Condenser Microphone
description:
The Rode NT1-A is renowned as one of the quietest studio condenser microphones on the market. Exceptionally low self-noise makes it ideal for capturing subtle vocal nuances and acoustic instruments.

Comes complete with the Rode SM6 shock mount and pop filter. A staple in Tachy's recording chain.
seoTitle: Rode NT1-A Condenser Microphone — Quietest Studio Mic by Tachy
seoDescription: Buy the Rode NT1-A condenser microphone. One of the quietest studio mics with only 5dBA self-noise. Perfect for vocals and acoustic recording.
features: Ultra-low self-noise of only 5dBA — near silent
Large 1-inch gold-sputtered diaphragm for rich tone
Cardioid polar pattern for focused sound capture
Complete package: SM6 shock mount, pop filter, XLR cable
Includes a 10-year manufacturer warranty
whyRecommend:
When I need the cleanest possible vocal recording, I reach for the NT1-A. The self-noise is so low that even in quiet passages, there's zero hiss. It captures the natural warmth and detail of my voice better than anything else in this price range.

The included SM6 shock mount is professional-grade — it isolates the mic from floor vibrations and desk bumps completely. If you record acoustic instruments or want pristine vocal takes, this is the mic for you.

faq.question: How does this compare to the AT2020?
faq.answer: The NT1-A has significantly lower self-noise (5dBA vs 20dBA) and includes a better shock mount. It's a step up in quality for about double the price.

faq.question: Does it require phantom power?
faq.answer: Yes, as a condenser microphone, the NT1-A requires 48V phantom power from your audio interface.

faq.question: Is the included shock mount good?
faq.answer: Yes, the Rode SM6 is one of the best shock mounts on the market. It effectively eliminates vibration noise and includes a pop filter.

name: M-Audio BX5 D3 Monitor Speakers
description:
The M-Audio BX5 D3 are 5-inch near-field studio monitors delivering accurate, flat frequency response for critical mixing and mastering.

Equipped with custom Kevlar woofers and natural silk tweeters. Tachy uses these paired with the AKG K240 for a complete monitoring setup.
seoTitle: M-Audio BX5 D3 — Studio Monitor Speakers by Tachy
seoDescription: Buy the M-Audio BX5 D3 near-field studio monitors. Kevlar woofers and silk tweeters for accurate mixing and mastering.
features: 5-inch Kevlar low-frequency driver for punchy bass
1-inch natural silk dome tweeter for smooth highs
45W + 25W bi-amped Class A/B amplification
Acoustic Space Control for room boundary compensation
Rear ported design for extended low-end response
whyRecommend:
Good monitors are essential for making good mix decisions. The BX5 D3s give me an honest picture of my mix — if something sounds good on these, it'll sound good anywhere.

The Kevlar woofers deliver tight, controlled bass that doesn't boom or exaggerate. Combined with my AKG K240 headphones, this setup lets me cross-reference my mixes with confidence.

faq.question: What size room are these suitable for?
faq.answer: The BX5 D3s are ideal for small to medium home studios (10-20 sq meters). For larger rooms, consider the BX8 D3s.

faq.question: Do I need a subwoofer?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The 5-inch drivers provide adequate bass response for mixing most genres. Add a sub if you produce bass-heavy music like EDM or hip-hop.

faq.question: What cables do I need?
faq.answer: You'll need two balanced TRS or XLR cables to connect these to your audio interface.
